filing_deadline_notes: Presumption does not apply to claims filed more than 84 months (7 years) after termination of nonvolunteer firefighter employment
notes: Applies only to NONVOLUNTEER firefighters (paid at or above state minimum wage). Expressly does NOT apply to volunteer firefighters. Diagnosis must be first by physician after July 1, 2009. Prostate cancer presumption does not apply if first diagnosed after age 55 (claimant may still prove without presumption). Tobacco rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence that tobacco was major contributing cause. Denial must be based on clear and convincing evidence condition was not caused or contributed to in material part by employment.

condition_specific: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) or acute stress disorder (DSM-5)
notes: ORS 656.802(7), enacted by SB 507 (effective September 29, 2019). Covers full-time paid firefighters, EMS providers, police officers, corrections/youth correction officers, parole/probation officers, and emergency dispatchers/9-1-1 operators. The condition is PTSD or acute stress disorder under DSM-5 criteria. Eligibility requires 5+ years of employment, or a single traumatic event meeting DSM-5 Criterion A, which waives the service requirement. The rebuttal standard is clear and convincing medical evidence that the person's duties were not of real importance in causing the condition. The claim window is 7 years, measured from either continued employment or separation.
